jobs_results.description:
Description

Amazon's Center for Quantum Computing in Pasadena, CA, is looking to hire a Hardware Development Engineer. You will join a multi-disciplinary team of experimental and theoretical physicists, materials scientists, and hardware and software engineers working at the forefront of quantum computing. We are looking for candidates who exemplify strong engineering principles, resourcefulness, a bias for action, exceptional problem-solving abilities, and really good communication skills. Working effectively within a team environment is essential. A robust background in physics or engineering is required. Effective day-to-day scripting skills are also critical for this role. Practical laboratory experience and a comprehensive grasp of experimental techniques and instrumentation are also necessary.

Key job responsibilities

A successful candidate will play a key role in our accelerated learning initiatives, requiring adept coordination with cross-functional stakeholders, meticulous execution of scientific measurements under established test standards, the production of clear and accurate documentation, streamlining of system integration, throughput optimization, and autonomous maintenance of assigned instruments. An ability to build, run, and debug automated measurement sequences is a key responsibility of this role.

Why AWS

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences.

Mentorship and Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic Qualifications

 Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, material science, physics or equivalent Knowledge of a scripting language (Python, R, etc.) Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities Knowledge of tools and measurement devices (oscilloscope, frequency analyzer, or equivalent)

Preferred Qualifications

 Experience working in a fast-paced, team environment Experience working with cryogenic systems

jobs_results.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 10/17/2026



Meet the Team  

The Outshift by Cisco team is one of Cisco’s most innovative organizations, driving the next generation of transformative technologies and business opportunities. As part of the Strategy, Incubation & Applications group led by Cisco’s Chief Strategy Officer, you will collaborate with some of the company’s most forward-thinking researchers, engineers, and technology leaders. Within the Outshift Quantum Research team and Quantum Labs, we are pioneering the design and development of practical, scalable, and efficient quantum networking technologies — building blocks for the future Quantum Internet. Our multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers is dedicated to advancing the state of the art in quantum networking, distributed quantum systems, and quantum-enabled applications.

  

Your Impact  

Cisco Quantum Research Team is seeking a Optomechanical  Engineer to support our Quantum Experimental Team that is central to the physical realization of Cisco's deployable quantum hardware platforms. In this role: 

You will take delicate breadboard and benchtop optical setups developed in R&D and re-engineer them into compact, vibration-isolated, and manufacturable 19-inch rack-mount chassis. 

You will solve critical thermal expansion, structural deformation, and drift challenges, maintaining sub-micron kinematic alignment across wide operating temperature and mechanical shock/vibration profiles. 

You will establish standardized mounting, fiber routing, and precision adjustment mechanisms that enable fast, repeatable assembly, testing, and servicing without requiring time-consuming manual alignment on customer sites. 

Design compact, modular, and ruggedized enclosures (1U–4U chassis) for precision free-space optics, fiber-to-chip interfaces, laser sources, and photonic devices. 

Design the layout of free-space optics, fiber-to-chip interfaces, laser sources, and photonic devices inside each enclosure capable of maintaining ultra-high alignment stability over extended operational lifespans. 

Perform Finite Element Analysis (FEA) for structural deformation, thermal expansion (CTE matching), and heat dissipation in enclosed optical modules. 

Design active and passive vibration isolation systems to protect sensitive optical paths from internal cooling fan vibrations and external data center acoustic/structural noise. 

Conduct comprehensive tolerance stack-up analyses (GD&T) to guarantee optical alignment budgets and component interchangeable assembly tolerances. 

Build, assemble, and validate initial optomechanical prototypes in the lab, testing for thermal drift, mechanical stability, optical loss, and vibration susceptibility. 

Collaborate with optical physicists and systems engineers to characterize insertion loss, beam quality, and phase stability across environmental stress screening (ESS). 

Work with vendors and machine shops to select specialized materials, precision machining methods, custom optical coatings, and surface finishes. 





Minimum Qualifications  

Bachelors + 8 years of related experience, or Masters + 6 years of related experience, or PhD + 3 years of related experience, or equivalent related work experience. 

2+ years experience in optomechanical design, precision mechanism design, or optoelectronic packaging for commercial, aerospace, or telecom applications. 

Experience in 3D CAD (SolidWorks, Creo) and FEA tools (ANSYS, COMSOL, or SolidWorks Simulation) for structural, thermal, and modal analysis. 

Experience with GD&T (ASME Y14.5), kinematic design principles, CTE matching techniques, and micron-level precision adjustment mechanisms. 

Experience packaging free-space optics, fiber launches, photonic devices, or laser assemblies into enclosed hardware products.  



Preferred Qualifications 

Experience with deployment of hybrid systems including free-space optics, fiber systems, integrated photonic device in data center environment. 

Experience with standard optical telecommunication components and architecture, as well as designing or operating optical data center rack systems. 

Experience with scaling quantum R&D prototypes into standardized, customer-ready 19 inch rack solution. 

Expereince in collaborating with systems engineers to perform co-dependent tolerance, thermal, and mechanical safety margin analyses across chassis and rack boundaries. 

Excellent communication skills with the ability to work effectively across scientific and engineering teams. 









Why Cisco? At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere. 

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

jobs_results.description:
Introduction

At IBM Research, we are the innovation engine of IBM. Exploring what’s next in computing and shaping the technologies the world will rely on tomorrow. From advancing AI and hybrid cloud to pioneering practical quantum computing, we anticipate challenges and unlock new opportunities for clients, partners, and society. Working in Research means joining a team that accelerates discovery at the intersection of high-performance computing, AI, quantum, and cloud. You’ll collaborate with leading scientists, engineers, and visionaries to push boundaries and turn ideas into reality. With a culture built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration, IBM Research offers the opportunity to grow your career while contributing to breakthroughs that transform industries and change the world.

Your Role And Responsibilities

At IBM Quantum we build utility scale (> 100 qubit) quantum computer systems comprised of superconducting qubits cooled to 10mK in dilution refridgerators and controlled by microwave pulses produced from advanced racks of room temperature electronics. Our team at IBM quantum working on building, deploying and calibrating these systems is looking for a summer intern on our subteam working on system assembly and test. In this role you will help build out our quantum systems by assembling mechanical and wiring components inside the dilution refridgerator. You will help test and troubleshoot those installations and perform investigative studies on methodologies to improve our assemblies.

Preferred Education

Bachelor's Degree

Required Technical And Professional Expertise

Candidate for this role is required to have the following expertise:

Studies in EE, Physics,Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science or a related disciplineProficient in electrical test and design of experimentsProgramming knowledge for test automationExperience troubleshooting complex systemsDesire/interest to work in the field of system assembling and validation

Preferred Technical And Professional Experience

Candidate for this role would also benefits from the following expertise:

General knowledge of microwave circuits, incl. components and test equipmentUnderstanding of circuit design principlesKnowledge of Python and linux shellExperience with cryogenic systems
